reviewer_summary.question: Why must a chosen word be processed before choosing another word, and which earlier calculations can each layer reuse?
reviewer_summary.takeaway: Choosing blue uses is’s finished result; processing blue makes a new result, while each layer reuses earlier keys and values because appending blue does not change their inputs.

findings.problem: Copying, clipping negatives, naming the positive part and preserving the original are introduced together; position has an unclear referent.

resolution.note: Separate keeping the original, starting a copy, applying the rule and naming its result into four visible beats. Use the word The rather than an unexplained position reference.

findings.problem: The addition beat also introduces the next general division rule before one division is shown.

resolution.note: Let the total beat only add amounts. The following beat shows one actual division and the resulting fraction.

findings.problem: Relative number is not concretely distinguishable from a fraction; 1.25 may mean 125 percent.

resolution.note: Explicitly identify the amount as an intermediate number; calculate shares only after both source amounts are ready.
